ETERNAL, 10 Jun – 10 Sep 2026 — MACD × Stoch RSI Settings on Every Chart (no ROC)

Rules (the no-ROC version from eternal_sep_oct_2026_check.md): buy at a candle close when the close is above EMA 50, the MACD histogram is bigger than the previous bar, and Stoch RSI blue crosses above orange with blue below 50 on that buy candle; sell the moment blue touches orange; trade again on the next signal; a trade still open on 10 Sep is sold at the last close. Delivery, ₹1,00,000 per trade, FYERS charges only. Education, not investment advice. Script ../../../projects/trading-equation-backtests/experiments/strategy5_window_sweep.py; all results and the top trades in reports/strategy5/window_sweep_eternal_2026-06-10_2026-09-10/.

Tried: MACD 12/26/9 (default), 8/21/5, 5/35/5, 19/39/9, 8/17/9, 24/52/18 × Stoch RSI K 2/3/5 × D 2/3/5 × RSI length 7/9/14/21 × stochastic length 7/9/14/21 = 864 settings per chart, on 15-min, 30-min, 1-hour, 4-hour, daily. ETERNAL rose +34.3% in the window (₹239.80 → ₹322.10), so holding it would have made about +₹34k on ₹1L.

Before the window the same setting made +₹58,793 on ETERNAL (28 trades), and +₹502 on 1 trade after it.

What it shows

  • Daily and 4-hour are robust for ETERNAL: most settings make money (698 and 463 of 864), and most of those also made money before the window. Faster Stoch settings (RSI/stochastic length 7–9, D 5) give more daily trades and catch more of the rise.
  • 15-min and 1-hour mostly lose: only 6–17% of settings make money, and most of those lose before the window. Their "best" settings are mostly luck.
  • Nothing beats simply holding ETERNAL here (+34%, ≈ +₹34k): the best daily setting caught +₹20.6k. Strong one-way rallies favour holding; this strategy steps in and out.
  • 864 settings on one stock and one window will always produce some great-looking numbers. Before using a setting, test it on Nifty 50 (the standard-setup tests found MACD 12/26/9 + Stoch 3/3/14/14 on daily to be the most consistent across all stocks).
